# 🌊 Fishing area analysis

The three fishing area functions describe one FAO major fishing area.
The examples use the **Eastern Central Atlantic (area 34)**; the last
section shows the same analysis for the **Northwest Pacific (area 61)**.

## 🗺️ The FAO major fishing areas

``` r

data <- load_fao_data()
areas <- aggregate(Production ~ FAO.major.fishing.area..Name., data = subset(data, Year == max(Year)), FUN = sum)
names(areas) <- c("Fishing area", "Catch in the last year (t)")
show_table(areas[order(-areas[[2]]), ], n = 30, digits = 0)
```

[`fishing_area_data()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_data.md).

## 1️⃣ `fishing_area_data()`: catch of the area

``` r

FAO34 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Eastern Central")
```

![fishing_trend.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/fishing_trend.png`

![fishing_percentage.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/fishing_percentage.png`

![area_country_map.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area_country_map.png`

It saves three charts:

| File | Chart |
|----|----|
| `fishing_trend.png` | Total catch of the area. With `timeseries_analysis = TRUE`, the grey bars are the mean catch of each period between **breakpoints** (dashed lines), found with [`strucchange::breakpoints()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/strucchange/man/breakpoints.html) |
| `fishing_percentage.png` | The area’s share of the world catch each year, and its average (red line) |
| `area_country_map.png` | Total catch of each country in the area over all years, on a world map |

and returns a list:

| Element | Content |
|----|----|
| `area_data` | Catch records of the area: the input of the other functions |
| `coefs_data` | Start, end and mean catch of each period between breakpoints |
| `act_world_map` | The map data (an sf object) |

``` r

FAO34$coefs_data
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   start_year end_year intercept
#>        <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1       1950     1968   724833.
#> 2       1969     1987  3005779.
#> 3       1988     2009  3682002.
#> 4       2010     2023  4890618.
```

### Options

``` r

fishing_area_data(
  "Atlantic, Eastern Central",
  timeseries_analysis = FALSE,          # no breakpoints
  area_color1 = "#9ecae1",              # fill of the catch area
  area_color2 = "#08519c",              # its outline
  hline_color = "#e6550d",              # average line of the share chart
  fill_scale = "blue",                  # palette of the map
  lang = "zh"                           # Chinese chart text
)
```

![fishing_trend.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/fishing_trend.png`

![fishing_percentage.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/fishing_percentage.png`

![area_country_map.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area_country_map.png`

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|----|----|----|
| `area_name` | FAO major fishing area |  |
| `plot` | Save charts | `TRUE` |
| `timeseries_analysis` | Add breakpoints to the catch chart | `TRUE` |
| `area_color1`, `area_color2`, `area_alpha` | Fill, outline and transparency of the catch area | `"grey80"`, `"black"`, `0.7` |
| `line_color`, `line_alpha`, `line_linewidth`, `point_size` | Line and points of the share chart | `"black"`, `0.8`, `1.5`, `2` |
| `hline_color`, `hline_alpha`, `hline_linewidth` | Average line of the share chart | `"red"`, `0.7`, `1.5` |
| `axis_text_size`, `axis_title_size`, `axis_text_face`, `axis_title_face` | Axis text | `10`, `12`, `"plain"`, `"bold"` |
| `polygon_color`, `fill_scale` | Country borders and palette of the map | `"grey90"`, map palette of [`fao_settings()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_settings.md) |
| `axis_title_size_map`, `axis_text_size_map`, `legend_text_size_map` | Text sizes of the map | `14`, `12`, `12` |
| `lang` | `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | language of [`fao_settings()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fao_settings.md) |
| `data_version` | FAO release: `"latest"`, `"bundled"` or e.g. `"2023.1.1"` | `"latest"` |
| `pptx` | Also save editable PowerPoint | `FALSE` |

## 2️⃣ `fishing_area_species()`: main species

``` r

species <- fishing_area_species(FAO34$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 10))
```

![area_species.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area/area_species.png`

![area_species_wrap.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area/area_species_wrap.png`

| File | Chart |
|----|----|
| `area/area_species.png` | Catch of the ten main species over time |
| `area/area_species_wrap.png` | One panel per species with its share of the area’s catch, a linear trend (dashed) and the breakpoints of its mean catch |

The function returns the catch by species and year, the ranking, and the
breakpoints:

``` r

show_table(species$area_species_ranked_total)
```

| ASFIS.species..Name.         | Total_Tonnes | Percentage |

It also saves two tables in `tables/`: `species_ranked_table.csv`
(average catch per decade, catch in the last five years, share in the
last year) and `species_coefs_data.csv` (breakpoints).

``` r

show_table(read.csv("tables/species_ranked_table.csv", fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM", check.names = FALSE), n = 5, digits = 0)
```

### Options

- **`rank_range`** chooses the ranks: `c(11, 20)` shows the next ten
  species.
- **`timeseries_analysis = FALSE`** replaces the breakpoints by a smooth
  curve (`smooth_method`, default `"loess"`).
- **`h_value`** is the minimum length of a period between breakpoints: a
  fraction of the series (default `0.15`) or a number of years
  (e.g. `5`). Larger values give fewer breakpoints; species with too
  short a series are skipped with a message.

``` r

fishing_area_species(FAO34$area_data, rank_range = c(11, 20), h_value = 5, lang = "both")
```

![area_species.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area/area_species.png`

![area_species_wrap.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area/area_species_wrap.png`

Style arguments: `line_width`, `point_size`, `point_alpha`,
`point_shape`, `line_alpha`, `axis_text_size`, `axis_title_size`,
`strip_text_size`, `axis_text_face`, `axis_title_face`,
`strip_text_face`, `smooth_method`, `smooth_linetype`, `line_linewidth`,
`text_hjust`, `text_vjust`, `text_size`, `text_color` and `facet_ncol`.

## 3️⃣ `fishing_area_country()`: main countries

``` r

countries <- fishing_area_country(FAO34$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 10))
```

![area_country.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area/area_country.png`

![area_country_wrap.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`figures/png/area/area_country_wrap.png`

It has the same arguments and outputs as
[`fishing_area_species()`](https://linbojun99.github.io/faofishingreport/reference/fishing_area_species.md),
by country (`area/area_country.png`, `area/area_country_wrap.png`,
`tables/country_ranked_table.csv`, `tables/country_coefs_data.csv`).

``` r

show_table(countries$area_country_ranked_total)
```

## 🌏 Another area: the Northwest Pacific

Any FAO area works the same way. The Northwest Pacific (area 61) is the
largest fishing area:

``` r

FAO61 <- fishing_area_data("Pacific, Northwest")
fishing_area_country(FAO61$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 8))
```

Charts of different areas are saved under the same file names
(e.g. `fishing_trend.png`), so use one working folder per area,
e.g. `setwd("reports/FAO61")`.
